answer: Anti-sybil standing is decided at the kernel of each account: lock a bond, then publish one original epoch artifact that independent grader seats score on the ledger. Only a passing score counts as peer-attested work; a slogan or copy does not. A cloned key is a new vertex that still must post its own bond and a unique passing write. Reused text collides by hash, grades collapse, and the bond is slashed. A farm branching like a willow therefore pays linearly in capital and fresh labor for every leaf, so mass clones stay unprofitable while one established identity remains cheap to maintain.
